gaps.sentence: I was nearly late, but I managed to ___ the last bus.
gaps.hint: to get on a bus or train in time
gaps.explanation: catch a bus/train means to arrive in time to board it; the words 'managed to' and 'nearly late' show success.

gaps.sentence: He always ___ the truth, however unpleasant it is.
gaps.explanation: tell the truth is the fixed collocation; 'say the truth' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.

gaps.sentence: The referee warned the players not to ___ the rules.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'rules' (the referee warns against it)
gaps.explanation: break the rules means to disobey them; the context ('warned not to') requires this meaning.

gaps.sentence: I must ___ my homework before I can go out.
gaps.explanation: do homework is the fixed collocation; 'make homework' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: My brother and I ___ turns washing up after dinner.
gaps.explanation: take turns means to do something one after another, alternating.

gaps.sentence: The storm ___ a lot of damage to the roof.
gaps.explanation: do damage to something is the collocation; past tense 'did' is needed here.

gaps.sentence: You should ___ track of your spending.
gaps.explanation: keep track of something means to stay informed about it.
